# Reviewer verdict: BLOCK

PR #330, round 1, exact head 1c998e75d005eaa70266314da25a533204ab7f70.
Answers 01a1ff60-567f-7460-8d91-6ab7a66f9a5c.

Two normal-use correctness/cost failures block this head. The requested D1-D3 mutations are independently killed; release ordering and cancellation controls pass.

## B330-01 [P1]: the fleet batch exceeds tmux's command-message ceiling

Location: crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1583-1639.

The adapter serializes every pending pane into one argv command list. tmux 3.6a checks that packed list against its 16 KiB message transport (`tmux/tmux@3.6a`, client.c:370-397; compat/imsg.h:30), not merely the host's ARG_MAX. A sufficiently large fleet is therefore rejected before ANY command executes. Verification sees every pipe/marker still live, so the same oversized list is launched again until the grace expires, with no progress.

Independent actual-adapter witness against the unchanged head: a minimum-width 300-entry list produced 34 failed launches in 2.053271291 s, ended with `command too long`, and retained pipe=1, the ownership marker and sink. The witness deliberately repeats one owned pane to avoid launching 300 background jobs. Any 300 distinct valid pane IDs make the command at least as large; this is an argument-scaling witness, not a claim that 300 live panes were created. The matching direct tmux invocation packed 17,098 argument bytes and was rejected. The host ARG_MAX was 1 MiB.

Required: use a transport that carries the supported fleet-sized batch, or otherwise bound the packed command size while preserving the intended cost contract. Never retry a structurally oversized command unchanged. Deduplicating this witness alone does not fix a real large fleet of distinct IDs.

## B330-02 [P2]: one permanently failing listed pane starves healthy later taps

Location: crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1583-1639; core contract at crates/core/src/ports.rs:1259-1270.

The command list stops at its first failed command. A genuinely removed pane disappears from the verification snapshot and can be pruned, so that transient case can progress. An exited pane retained by tmux's normal `remain-on-exit` option is different: `pipe-pane` says `target pane has exited`, while the pane/pipe/marker remains listed. `pending.retain` retains it ahead of the untouched healthy suffix. Every retry fails at the same pane, and healthy later taps never run.

Independent three-pane actual-adapter witness: first live tap detached; retained exited middle pane failed; last LIVE tap failed to detach. There were 46 launches in 2.048724458 s, and the last live pane retained pipe=1, its ownership marker and sink. This violates the explicit contract that one pane's failure never keeps another tap attached; the former per-pane loop continued after an individual error.

Required: isolate per-pane command failures so other owned taps still execute, then verify/report each result. Retain only genuinely unsuccessful taps, rather than replaying a permanently failing head of the batch. This method also backs the single-pane retirement path, so permanent failures must not become repeated failed process launches there either.

## Other requested checks

- POLICY vs BRAKES: ownership still decides which taps may be detached. Verification and the retry deadline are BRAKES that retain a marker/sink or report failure; neither authorizes a foreign detach or introduces an age/retention policy.
- Ownership/quoting: no new shell interpolation was added. Detach receives separate OsString arguments; pane targets come from the tmux snapshot, and sink paths are not command text. Local ownership or the matching expected marker remains the existing authority. The healthy real-tmux 32-pane control leaves the foreign tap untouched and launches exactly once. This does not add a stronger guarantee against a foreign replacement after an ownership snapshot.
- Release order: passed an independent call of the actual `Daemon::shutdown` wiring with a recording fake backend. Normal trace is detach then release. Injecting a panic into the observer's joined task returns the observer error, but release still executes. This is wiring/exception proof, not a fleet-scale timing witness.
- AbortOnDrop: generic phase ownership/cancellation control passed; D2 with abort disabled failed its held-work witness. Abort occurs at cancellation points; already-running synchronous or spawn_blocking work is not forcibly interrupted.
- HTTP timing: the phase task is created immediately after the stop signal; the private shutdown receipt logs HTTP drain before park notices end, rather than only when the later join begins.
- D3/rendering and the #325 scope/cooldown documentation are checked; the raw-seat-ID mutant failed the grammar witness.
- Two seconds is convergence/retry grace, not a hard child or shutdown timeout: deadline checking follows blocking command execution and verification reads. Retrying is for any residual pipe OR marker, not only panes closed mid-list. The claimed one-launch cost is the healthy branch only. Performance's supplemental BLOCK (da449fe) supersedes its initial pass-with-notes after verifying these two receipts.
- Fleet BEFORE/AFTER: the supplied BEFORE is 4731 ms at about 145 panes. AFTER on an authorized deployed bounce remains owed; no working-seat mutation or fleet bounce was induced here.
- Merge: GitHub reported DIRTY against main 85fe143e51c5df598ff27c87c88fd222d44cf43f. This head must be reconciled and re-frozen; it is not merge-clean/FINAL merely because all five latest checks passed.

## Evidence

Original-source baseline ran from a git archive of the exact head through `just shared-build`, canonical shared target, niceness 19, four jobs and no incremental compilation.

|---|---|
| `just shared-build -- clippy --locked -p pij-core -p pij-testkit -p pij-tmux -p pij-daemon --all-targets -- -D warnings` | macOS passed |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-tmux --test control_mode detaching_many_taps_launches_once_and_leaves_a_foreign_tap_alone -- --exact --nocapture` | Original healthy 32-pane control passed: one launch, foreign tap spared |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib store_shutdown_tests -- --nocapture` | 3/3 passed |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib death_sweep -- --nocapture` | 9/9 passed |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib pane_observer::tests::tombstoning_an_observed_seat_detaches_marker_and_captured_bytes -- --exact --nocapture` | Passed |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-tmux --test control_mode review_ -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` | Exit 101, TWO intended regression assertions failed: B330-01 and B330-02; measured counts/time/retained state in pr330-adapter-probes.log |
| `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib pane_observer::tests::review -- --nocapture` | Actual shutdown normal/panic recording-backend probe passed |
| Copied test binary, D1 per-pane launch | Exit 101: 30 launches versus 1, intended 32-pane assertion |
| Copied test binary, D2 no AbortOnDrop abort | Exit 101: cancelled phase still holds work, intended cancellation assertion |
| Copied test binary, D3 raw seat IDs | Exit 101: intended alarm grammar assertion |
| CI 44935479023/job 136941029721, artifact 14719931072 | Five focused exact-head original controls independently parsed as passed; CI does not contain the two new regression witnesses |
| `harness boot`; `harness checks --quick` | Boot ready=false; quick gate exit 1 from eight dependency/ambient-tool failures; heavy stages skipped, native/SDK/skill checks passed |

The 34/46-launch receipt ran BEFORE any D1/D2/D3 mutation selectors existed: only the added review tests and their real Tokio executor differed. Its adapter blob was the head's 164fc6e75e433c9e199f0ea91dcb1b3c1b848a95. The first attempt with a lightweight executor failed for lack of a Tokio reactor and was corrected; that fixture failure is not product evidence. All three mutation-off controls passed before the independent mutant runs. Test binaries were copied out under the shared-build lock.

C25: no dependency links/installs and no local green full-ship claim. All product worktrees remain untouched; review instrumentation is restored byte-identically before named cleanup. Receipts remain in session artifacts: pr330-baseline.log, pr330-transport-probe.log, pr330-adapter-probes.log, pr330-order-and-controls.log, pr330-d1.log, pr330-d2.log, pr330-d3.log and pr330-harness-checks.log. The two regression fixtures are preserved for the fix owner as pr330-regression-tests.rs.

Harness magicWand: keep fleet-size transport and permanent-command-failure witnesses beside the healthy batch, and keep normal return, panic, cancellation and timer-origin claims separate. Green healthy-branch tests missed both failed-launch loops.

Hold reviewer/330 until merge. Round 2 should check these fixes and the reconciled exact head, not broaden the review.
